claims.statement: GS1 EANCOM remains a maintained standard for transaction flows, and GS1 EDI supports order, delivery, invoice, settlement, and remittance messages that can make order-to-cash paperless.

The GS1 Claims Notification guide already includes adjustment codes for trade and promotion discounts, incorrect references, incorrect charges, tax differences, advertising costs, and incorrect product identification.

SAP Revenue Growth Management Claims processes retailer deduction claims arising from promotional agreements, links a claim to a condition contract and source document, and validates the request against contractual terms.

SAP Dispute Management is designed for customer underpayments and discrepancies, copying accounting information into a case and supporting investigation, workflow, correspondence, and cross-organizational handling.

HighRadius documents automated claim capture from retailer portals, email, and EDI; item-level matching to trade promotions and external POS data; evidence assembly; dispute submission; and updates to ERP and trade-promotion systems.

Vistex documents automated validation and reconciliation of billback, scanback, and chargeback claims, with settlement through payments, credits, or deductions inside an integrated trade-promotion suite.

A Vistex-published case study says a 200-plus-employee food producer used SAP Paybacks and Chargebacks by Vistex and reported a 50% reduction in time to clear undetermined deductions plus lower administrative cost; this is vendor-reported evidence, not an independent causal study.

Inmar describes a recurring supplier workflow in which AR teams retrieve claim material from retailer or distributor portals, work within retailer-specific dispute windows, and use software to aggregate and prioritize deductions.

Polish unfair-contractual-advantage rules for agricultural and food supply prohibit unjustified reductions after accepted delivery and allow specified marketing, advertising, storage, or display charges only if clearly agreed in advance.
Mandatory KSeF invoice receipt began in Poland on 1 February 2026, and mandatory issuance was phased from February and April 2026, making structured invoice data a weaker standalone differentiation.

KSeF does not by itself provide promotion contracts, remittance explanations, retailer-portal backup, sell-out or proof-of-performance evidence, or the human resolution outcome, so those joins remain a possible workflow gap.

Because standards and incumbents already cover basic matching and claims workflow, a plausible entrant wedge is limited to a supplier-authorized historical audit and retailer-specific evidence layer that proves incremental recovery or lower handling cost in an account whose existing stack leaves a measurable gap.
The incidence, value, and recoverability of trade-promotion deductions for mid-sized Polish and CEE suppliers are not established by the reviewed public evidence.

No reviewed evidence establishes the target budget owner, willingness to authorize portal and ERP access, subscription or success-fee price, attribution method, conversion rate, retention, or service margin.
No reviewed evidence supports the candidate's earlier payback, customer-count, gross-margin, ARR, valuation, or founder-wealth timing scenarios.

contrary_evidence: [s10-01, s10-02, s10-03] GS1 already standardizes the order-to-cash sequence, commercial disputes, and detailed claim reason codes, reducing novelty in message normalization.
[s10-04, s10-05] SAP directly covers promotion-linked claim validation and receivables dispute workflows inside the system of record.
[s10-06] HighRadius markets nearly the full proposed supplier-side data and resolution flow, including retailer portal retrieval, promotion matching, evidence packets, disputes, and ERP updates.
[s10-07] Vistex bundles claims validation, reconciliation, settlement, credits, and deductions with trade-promotion management.
[s10-08] A vendor case study documents incumbent use by a 200-plus-employee food producer, weakening the premise that mid-sized suppliers are necessarily underserved.
[s10-09] Inmar already offers a SaaS deductions product centered on retailer-portal aggregation and AR review.
[s10-11] KSeF makes Polish invoice capture increasingly structured, removing part of the document-extraction wedge.
All quantitative recovery evidence reviewed is vendor-published and primarily outside Poland or CEE; it cannot validate local willingness to pay or the candidate's unit economics.

unknowns: Distribution of promotion deductions by value, reason, age, recoverability, and retailer among mid-sized Polish and CEE suppliers.
Whether target suppliers' existing ERP, EDI, TPM, advisers, or staff already resolve the highest-value cases economically.
Exact buyer and budget authority across accounts receivable, finance, key-account sales, revenue-growth management, and ownership.
Contractual and technical permission to use retailer portals, credentials, remittance files, sell-out data, promotion terms, and proof-of-performance documents.
Retailer-specific dispute windows, submission channels, evidence acceptance, and change frequency in Poland and CEE.
A defensible baseline for attributing recovered cash or avoided labor to the product rather than ordinary staff action or later credits.
Public or buyer-validated pricing, implementation effort, support load, sales cycle, procurement requirements, gross margin, and retention.
How much human finance or legal review is mandatory and whether that requirement prevents software-like margins.
Independent clearance of the founder's employment conflict, confidentiality, non-solicitation, and adjacent-market restrictions.
Any evidence-backed route or timing to the founder's net-worth objective.
